main_body: A roofed well: snow-covered roof, two wooden posts, a stone rim with a dark water opening and a bucket, and a striped stone base below.
top_band: At x=15 the well rim and opening start at row 16 (light rim, L=80-249) and the dark ellipse runs rows 17-22 (L=20-58, with a bucket at rows 17-19). A light front lip sits at row 23 (L=145). Above, the snow roof (rows 1-8, L=166-249) is a light horizontal surface.
evidence: The well mouth is a clear ellipse seen from above: a light back rim, a dark interior with a brown bucket, and a lighter front lip at row 23, which reads as a visible top surface. Below it the stone front face (rows 24-30, about 7 rows) is banded in dark and mid grey. The snow roof is also a light top band over posts with icicle fringes. The posts and the dark ellipse are inset behind the roof, which gives the eave shadow. This matches the reference roofed well, so it is a correct 3/4 construction.

style.evidence: The snow ramp has about 6 steps (#f6f9fd, #dce5f1, #bccade, #97a8c6, #7383a8, #55628a). The stone and wood each carry several tones. The outlines are tinted dark blue and brown, and only 0% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so there is no sticker look. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, with stone-block texture on the wall and grain on the posts. At 14 colours per tile and 24 distinct colours it is below the references (17-20 per tile, 38-40 colours), and the stone base stripes are somewhat simple. It would still sit acceptably next to the reference.
